To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) DNA replication initiation in human cells occurs in a genome-wide manner and is highly dynamic; (ii) DNA replication initiation occurs in two waves in human cells, with the first wave being more dynamic than the second one; (iii) DNA replication initiation is regulated by the chromosomal context, and (iv) deregulation of DNA replication initiation is associated with abnormal cell proliferation.

1) the activation of origins of replication in human cells is a highly dynamic process, 2) the activation of a given origin is a stochastic process, 3) there is no correlation between the level of activation and the level of transcription of an origin, 4) the activation of an origin is a highly regulated process and 5) the deregulation of this process can lead to abnormal proliferation.
